status: Adopted 2026-10-25 (AQ-042): pooled revision option (ii) cap+A2, configuration A (California in the common level); Madison on the observed Madison-like path
units: second-home permits on single-family lots per 1,000 one-unit detached homes per year

area_levels.basis: pooled two-stage model across California (cap of 2 ADUs per parcel plus the A2 multifamily parcel rule, AQ-041), seven statewide-law states and five cities, with the vacant-lot new-house factor x(1 - 0.049) on non-California series (AQ-039) and Minneapolis x(1 - 0.127); written by scripts/run_pooled_revision.py (docs/gate3/POOLED_REVISION.md)

madison_floor.units: second-home permits on single-family lots per 1,000 one-unit detached homes per year; applied to every area and path by the engine (AQ-024)

g3f_revision_2026_10_25.basis: Madison 2022-2025: 40 second-home units / 213.168 thousand home-years (53,292 one-unit detached homes x 4 years) = 0.1876, divided by 0.8 = 0.2345 (docs/gate3/POOLED_REVISION.md)

lower.basis: Like the slower statewide-law states: pooled revision (ii) configuration A, 10th percentile of the between-state spread (factor 1/1.89)
lower.label: Like the slower statewide-law states
lower.info: Below every statewide-law state's typical level; the closest are Rhode Island and Oregon.

central.basis: Like a typical statewide-law state: pooled revision (ii) configuration A central; ramp from the pooled year terms
central.label: Like a typical statewide-law state

upper.basis: Strong adoption: pooled revision (ii) configuration A, 90th percentile of the between-state spread (factor 1.89). The high end of what statewide-law states have reached; only California has gone higher.
upper.label: Strong adoption
upper.info: The high end of what statewide-law states have reached; only California has gone higher.

madison_like_path.units: second-home permits on single-family lots per 1,000 one-unit detached homes per year, forecast years 1-5 (2027-2031); already ramped, so the engine applies no ramp on top
madison_like_path.source: reference/madison_like_median_path.csv, group 'WA+OR Madison-like (main)': median of 9 Washington and Oregon Madison-like cities in years 1-3 and 4 Oregon cities in years 4-5 (docs/gate3/MADISON_LIKE_CITIES.md)
madison_like_path.basis: Owner decision 2026-10-25 (AQ-040 follow-up, AQ-042): Madison, the only Wisconsin place meeting the Madison-like definition (incorporated; 20,000-120,000 one-unit detached homes; median value $250,000-$500,000; not the largest city), follows the observed Madison-like path instead of its pooled level.

statewide_adoption_line: reference/pooled_revision_adoption_line.csv, variant vacant_lot_x0.951 (median observed path of statewide-law states with the AQ-039 vacant-lot factor; shown alongside the scenarios). The as-reported line is in the same file; reference/statewide_adoption_curve.csv is the 2026-10-24 version.
notes: Uniform 'level' (the Madison floor) applies only where an area has no model level. The Madison floor is set once, in madison_floor (in_use selects the variant; every path and script reads it via missing_middleware.model.params.madison_floor). area_paths replaces an area's level and ramp with an explicit observed path (engine.run area_paths). The California ramp is not applied on top of the pooled ramp. Path-specific ramps reproduce the pooled model's direct totals (each path scales the whole rate path); rounded to 4 decimals.
